en.title: Maximum Chain Reaction from Detonating One Bomb
en.description:
When bomb i explodes, it detonates every bomb within distance r[i] of it, and the chain reaction continues. Choose the first bomb to detonate and find the maximum number of bombs detonated; since the radii differ, propagation is directed.

The standard input/output is compiled by CSWork; numeric ranges marked as this site's are this site's judging conventions.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..1000); then n lines with x y r, −100000≤x,y≤100000, 1≤r≤100000.
en.output: Output the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: detonate the second bomb first; its radius 4 directly detonates the other two, for 3 in total. It is not the case that the third bomb can detonate the second. Example 2: the two bombs do not affect each other, so the maximum is 1. Example 3: the first bomb covers the other two, for 3 in total.
hints: First compute directed adjacency bitsets (including the bomb itself), use a bitset version of transitive closure to merge all points reachable through each intermediate point, and finally take the maximum number of set bits.
